chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:

If you find the price of the sacrificial animal but do not find the sacrificial animal, then leave the price with a man from the people of Mecca so that he may buy it for you in Dhu al-Hijjah and slaughter it on your behalf. If Dhu al-Hijjah passes and he has not bought it, he should postpone it until the next Dhu al-Hijjah, because the days of slaughter have passed.

key_terms.أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ: the people of Mecca, from among whom an agent may be appointed
key_terms.أَيَّامَ الذَّبْحِ: the designated days in which the sacrifice may validly be slaughtered
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial animal offered in hajj
key_terms.ثَمَنَ: the price or monetary value to be paid
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, during which the sacrifice is performed
key_terms.وَيَذْبَحَهُ: and slaughter it, meaning perform the sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he can afford the hady but cannot find a sacrificial animal during Dhu al-Hijjah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamatti' who has the money for the hady but cannot obtain the animal itself. It instructs him to entrust the payment to someone in Mecca to purchase and slaughter it in Dhu al-Hijjah, and if that is not done before the slaughter days end, it is deferred until the following Dhu al-Hijjah.
